newsitem.title: CROATIA: Dearth of kuna raises Croatian interbank rates.
newsitem.headline: Dearth of kuna raises Croatian interbank rates.

text.p: Lack of kuna funds raised all Croatian interbank rates in mid-morning trade on Friday ahead of holiday spending, money dealers said.
Call money rose to 10 percent from 9.0 percent previously and seven-day funds were sold at 11 percent, up from 10.
One 90-day loan was struck at 17 percent, and lenders were also said to have charged extra costs on top of interest.
"If there had been money available today, borrowers would have paid even more," said one dealer.
She said even those banks that usually appear on the supply side sought kuna, making trade "more like scrounging".
Today's payment by the central bank to the banks which sold it hard currency two days ago helped little as they apparently needed all the kuna for their own business.
As demand boomed on Thursday night, total borrowing through the market topped 63 million kuna. The central bank also intervened with a 13.4 million kuna Lombard loan at 11 percent.
Overnight trade was done at a single rate of 8.1 percent, one percentage point below the day's average. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
